explanation: Any vector can be split into a horizontal piece vx and a vertical piece vy that, placed tip-to-tail, rebuild it exactly. Because the vector is the hypotenuse of a right triangle, vx = |v|·cos(theta) (the adjacent side) and vy = |v|·sin(theta) (the opposite side). Drag the magnitude to lengthen the arrow and the angle to rotate it; the green and purple legs stretch and shrink as the components change.
bullets: vx is the shadow on the x-axis (|v|·cos theta); vy is the shadow on the y-axis (|v|·sin theta).
The vector, vx, and vy form a right triangle: vx and vy are the legs, v is the hypotenuse.
At theta = 0 the vector is all horizontal; at 90° it is all vertical.
